title: Cross-border request redaction and evidence notebook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working notebook for operators, SREs, and legal contacts to triage, redact, and package evidence when we receive cross-border data requests (subpoena/DSAR/administrative request) that mention or touch tenant data routed by region pins. The goal: provide a repeatable operator script that preserves auditability, minimizes exposure, and produces an evidentiary bundle acceptable to internal legal review and customer-facing incident response.

Context notes (quick):
- We run mixed-hosted/dedicated/private customers; private tenants can have region anchors and soft fallbacks.
- Evidence commonly needs: request copy, routing decisions, server-side request logs, tenant pin metadata, storage location manifests, KMS key IDs, export hashes, redaction justification notes.
- Legal needs a defensible redaction trail (what, who, why, when) + checksum-able artifacts.

Operator playbook (step-by-step)
1) Intake and initial validation (T+0–15m)
   - Confirm request type (subpoena, DSAR, government admin). Tag with intake code.
   - Capture original request PDF/URL and place in secure intake folder (do not forward via Slack).
   - Open Jira ticket with prefix RES-CB-{date} and assign legal + oncall. Example: RES-CB-20241103-02.

2) Quick routing check (T+15–45m)
   - Query tenant metadata: tenant.region_pin, tenant.anchor_region, tenant.fallback_policy.
   - Check serving logs: route decisions for the request UUID (if request originated through API).
   - If routing shows cross-border fallback, mark as "possible-exposure" and escalate to legal immediately.

3) Evidence capture (preserve immutability)
   - Snapshot relevant routing traces (trace ids, spans) and save as gzipped JSON with SHA256.
   - Export object storage manifests (paths and object IDs) where related data resides.
   - Capture KMS audit entries (key usage logs) for the time window.
   - Record operator actions in the ticket with timestamp and username (must be human-readable).

4) Redaction-first approach (if legal authorizes partial disclosure)
   - Work with Legal to define redaction rules: token-level, field-level, or file-level.
   - Use the redaction CLI tool (redwood-residency-redact v0.9) in sandbox mode first: 
       redact --mode field --rules /rules/RES-CB-<id>-rules.json --input <object> --output <redacted>
   - Save both original and redacted versions in the evidence bucket; encrypt with case-specific ephemeral key (KMS key tag: RES-CB-<id>).
   - Compute and store checksums for original + redacted artifacts; add to evidence manifest.

5) Packaging and chain-of-custody notes
   - Prepare evidence bundle: request.pdf, request_metadata.json (routing+trace), storage_manifest.csv, kms_usage.csv, original_objects_hashlist.txt, redacted_objects_hashlist.txt, operator_log.txt.
   - Create a chain-of-custody file: who accessed what, when, from which host. Sign-off fields for operator + legal reviewer.

6) Customer communication template (if customer-facing required)
   - Draft note that confirms request received, high-level exposure assessment (no PII specifics), timeline for evidence release, and contact for follow-ups.
   - Use the template: RES-CB-CUSTOMER-ACK-v1. Edit to include TEID and ticket link.

Quick checklists (copyable)
- Intake copy saved: [ ]
- Jira created & legal looped: [ ]
- Tenant pin metadata snapshot saved: [ ]
- Traces exported & checksummed: [ ]
- KMS logs extracted: [ ]
- Originals encrypted & archived: [ ]
- Redacted outputs & checksums: [ ]
- Evidence bundle uploaded & chain-of-custody updated: [ ]
- Customer notification drafted (if applicable): [ ]

Telemetry and signals to collect (for postmortem)
- Frequency of cross-border fallbacks per tenant over 30d (query: telemetry.routing.fallbacks.count).
- Correlation of fallback events with config changes / deploys.
- Time-to-evidence (TTE): intake->bundle delivery. Target <72h.
- Redaction failure modes: missing rules, tool crash, KMS permission error.

Operator scripts / sample commands
- Snapshot traces (requires infra role): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://traces.internal/api/trace/<trace_id> | gzip > trace-<id>.json.gz && sha256sum trace-<id>.json.gz > trace-<id>.sha256
- Export storage manifest (S3-like): aws s3api list-objects --bucket tenant-archive-<tenant> --prefix 2024/11/ --output json > storage-manifest.json && jq -r '.Contents[].Key' storage-manifest.json > storage_manifest.csv
- Redact with dry-run: redwood-residency-redact --dry-run --rules rules.json --input storage-manifest.json --output redacted-manifest.json

Evidence packaging format (recommended)
- Bundle layout:
   /RES-CB-<id>/
     request.pdf
     request_metadata.json
     storage_manifest.csv
     original_objects_hashlist.txt
     redacted_objects_hashlist.txt
     chain_of_custody.txt
     kms_usage.csv

Notes & open questions (TODOs)
- Need an automated extractor that can assemble the manifest from trace ids — currently manual and error-prone. (See JIRA-RES-1287).
- Decide retention policy for redaction intermediate artifacts (how long do we keep originals vs redacted?). Legal wants originals kept for audit but ops wants shorter TTL.
- Could we add a soft-flag on tenant metadata: allow-legal-extract: true/false to short-circuit manual checks? Risks: consent/contract implications.
- Can we centralize ephemeral evidence keys in a short-lived keyring to reduce operator KMS sprawl?

References and past incidents
- RES-2024-07: cross-border fallback that required whole-tenant export (postmortem linked in CONFLUENCE-RESIDENCY-45).
- Slack thread: #residency-ops "gov request handling" (November 2024)

Notes to self (messy):
- When in doubt, escalate to legal early.
- Keep operator notes blunt and factual — avoid speculation in the chain-of-custody.
- If evidence contains aggregated PII that is not requested, redact aggressively and document rationale.

Appendix: redaction decision matrix (brief)
- Request asks for specific user: provide minimal context and user-level objects after legal OK.
- Request asks for tenant-wide logs: prefer providing derived metrics or redacted exports.
- Request unclear: push back with clarification and log the queries.

End of working notebook. This file is intentionally a "living" doc: update when tooling (redwood-residency-redact) changes, when legal updates standard rules, or after each RES-CB incident to capture lessons learned.
